_comment: protocol §8 — constants derived on THIS device. Peaks marked null are measured in T005/E1 and must not be filled from a spec sheet.
board_model: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin Developer Kit
multi_processor_count_READ_THIS_FIRST: null on purpose. On Orin the SM count depends on the power mode: TPC power gating removes SMs, and CUDA reports only the ungated ones. Use multi_processor_count_by_power_mode[<mode recorded for your run>]. The Orin AGX 64GB has 8 TPCs x 2 SMs = 16 SMs when no TPC is gated (MAXN / MODE_50W).

multi_processor_count_by_power_mode._source: TPC_PG_MASK per mode from /etc/nvpmodel.conf (see nvpmodel_modes.csv); 2 SMs per TPC. Only the mode this run was taken in is OBSERVED; the others are derived from the mask and must be confirmed by running in them.

device_state_when_recorded.warning: multi_processor_count and the peaks depend on the power mode: TPC power gating removes SMs. Record the mode with every use.

max_warps_per_sm_source: torch max_threads_per_multi_processor / 32 (1536/32 = 48); not taken from ncu

measured_peaks._method: CUDA-event timing, median of 100 calls after 20 warm-ups, MAXN, jetson_clocks applied, GPU clock pinned at 1300500000 Hz; every GEMM verified against an fp32 reference before its time was used. See this run's latency_summary.csv.
measured_peaks.peak_int8_CAVEAT: torch._int_mm does not reach the tensor cores on sm_87; this is a PyTorch-path throughput, NOT the hardware's dense INT8 peak. Do not use it as a hardware constant.

expected_from_spec_do_not_use_as_measure.source: docs/00_context.md / NVIDIA AGX Orin 64GB spec; LPDDR5-6400, 256-bit

ncu_per_sm_limits._warning: Everything under per_kernel_NOT_a_device_limit describes the ONE kernel this export holds (the T001 toy GEMM: 158 registers/thread, 49 KB static + 24.6 KB dynamic shared memory). Those numbers are properties of that launch, not of the GPU. Do not read them as hardware constants.
ncu_per_sm_limits.dram_note: 0. ncu --query-metrics offers 4426 metrics on this device and none is dram__*; an explicit --metrics dram__bytes.sum returns 'n/a'. See results/<run>/raw/ncu_dram_probe.log.

efficiency_fractions._purpose: docs/00_context.md carries these as **[ASSUMPTION]** in E11's analytic host model (`achieved_tflops = peak x eff_flops_frac`, `achieved_bw_GBps = ext_bw x eff_bw_frac`). These are the measured values. Both assumptions are pessimistic.
efficiency_fractions._caveat: Measured on dense square GEMM and a streaming kernel — the best case. The action expert's own shapes are small and skinny and do far worse; E2 (micro_ae_kernels.py) measures what THOSE shapes achieve.
